round_two_note: I asked for covenant terms and headroom. The research loop returned the instruments but not a single test. What it did recover is materially favourable and I am moving my downside score for it: the Senior Notes were repriced from Adjusted Term SOFR + 6.50% to + 4.75% and extended from 2030-06-23 to 2031-05-20, the revolver is undrawn, and debt fell from $231.425m actual to $75.0m as-adjusted and possibly $68.7m after an April 2026 prepayment. Lenders repricing a credit downward by 175 basis points while extending maturity is a real signal about how the debt is viewed. It changes my assessment of solvency risk. It does not change my vote, because my vote was never about solvency - it is about paying 2.7x PV-10 for a depleting asset on a gas deck that has already recovered.

explanatory_strength.rationale: Unchanged. Seniority is respected and the claims are not double-counted, but neither component moves the commodity price across the three cases. Both hold the $3.387/MMBtu SEC deck fixed, so the variable that determines whether this credit and this equity are money-good never varies. The stated range measures decline, discount rate and ownership uncertainty only.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Held at 2. The research loop confirmed that no covenant test, no restricted-payment basket and no headroom calculation exists anywhere in the packet - the dividend restriction is referenced in the prospectus but never specified. Nothing here has survived a reporting cycle: no 10-Q or 10-K since the 2026-06-10 IPO, companyfacts carrying only S-1 fee-table concepts, every operating figure pro forma, and a frozen adversarial pass that reconciled nothing.

downside_control.rationale: Raised from 2. The debt facts recovered in the research loop are better than the packet's headline suggested. Net debt of roughly $58m to $64m against $64.405m of pro forma Adjusted EBITDA is about 1.0x or below, the revolver is undrawn, maturity is 2031, and the repricing to SOFR + 4.75% means refinancing risk is remote for five years. A royalty funds no drilling capital, no lease operating expense and no plugging liability, so a price decline compresses cash flow without threatening solvency. It is not higher than 3 because the reserve book depletes on an 8.4-year life while the debt does not amortise with it, so leverage rises mechanically unless acquisitions replace reserves - and acquisitions are the first thing a tighter market removes.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Unchanged. Negative 19.53% annualised on the base with no positive case in the range. Better credit terms improve the odds of surviving to collect a bad return; they do not make the return good. The cycle framing still cuts against the position: 2.7x PV-10 is being paid on a $3.387/MMBtu deck that is already 59% above the $2.13 deck of the prior reserve report, so the multiple sits on top of a recovered price rather than a depressed one.

strongest_counter_explanation: Strengthened by the research loop and I want it on the record. This is a royalty, not an operator: no drilling capital, no lease operating expense, no plugging and abandonment liability, and therefore no maintenance obligation that a downturn makes unaffordable. At or below 1.0x leverage, undrawn revolver, 2031 maturity and a rate the lenders just cut by 175 basis points, this is a defensively financed entity. On that reading the cyclical risk belongs in the 9% to 12% discount rate the contract already applies, and pricing it a second time through my vote double-counts the same risk. The honest version of my position is that I am voting on price, not on credit - and a committee member voting on price from the credit-cycle seat should say so plainly.
most_important_missing_fact: The covenant terms of the Senior Notes and Revolving Credit Facility - leverage and coverage tests, the restricted-payment basket governing dividends, and current headroom - which determine whether a gas price decline forces a distribution cut before it threatens anything else. The research loop established this is not in the packet; it requires the first 10-Q's debt footnote or the filed credit agreements.
falsifiers: A covenant schedule showing restricted-payment and leverage headroom wide enough to sustain distributions through a $2.13/MMBtu deck.
The first 10-Q showing actual operating cash flow converging toward the CAFD run-rate rather than the $9.533m pro forma figure, which would mean the add-backs are genuinely non-recurring.
A demonstrated acquisition track record replacing reserves accretively through a full gas cycle rather than the twelve-month PHX and TRR window.
specialist_findings: The contract holds the SEC price deck fixed across all three cases, so for an unhedged royalty the stated range is narrower than the true distribution. The elasticity is measurable from the packet: $2.13/MMBtu produced $0.827 per Mcfe of PV-10 and $3.387 produced $1.422, so a 59% price move drove a 72% move in value per unit.

Applying that elasticity, a return to the prior deck would take PV-10 from $293.690m toward roughly $170m, which at 82.1% and net of claims puts Class A asset value near or below $2 per share. That downside case exists in no component of this contract.

The pro forma preferred dividend deduction of $7.076m equals the historical FY2025 figure exactly and appears unadjusted for the Series D redemption completed with IPO proceeds, making pro forma CAFD conservative on that line by roughly $4m to $5m.

The earnout is struck on Adjusted EBITDA targets the company defines and reports, on a measure already carrying $21.8m of fee add-backs, four months after a restatement in management-fee recording. That is the governance exposure sitting directly on the metric the credit is judged by.
